quickSteps: Create a new project and name it now
Confirm timeline resolution and frame rate
Set up automatic saving and project backup
proSteps: Ask first about the final deliverable: landscape or portrait, resolution, frame rate, HDR or SDR.
Set the timeline frame rate in Project Settings > Main Settings; changing it after importing the material may be restricted.
Use DaVinci YRGB Color Managed for small SDR projects; when in doubt start with Rec.709 Gamma 2.4 to deliver the target.
Set the working folder, cache, proxy and still frame locations to a high-speed disk with sufficient capacity.
Turn on real-time saving and set the interval and retention quantity of project backups.
Create media pool folders such as 01_MEDIA, 02_AUDIO, 03_GFX, 04_TIMELINES, 99_EXPORTS, etc.
mistake: Randomly changing the timeline frame rate of the pilot material may cause irreversible rhythm problems.
doneCheck: Timeline frame rate, resolution, color management, backup and cache locations are confirmed.
proNotes: Frame rate is a project level decision
Output transformation can only be done once

quickSteps: Copy footage and keep card directory
proSteps: The camera card is copied completely according to the original directory, not only the video files are dragged away; at least two independent copies are kept.
Import on the media page and check for offline, damaged, abnormal frame rates and audio channels.
Create a searchable structure using metadata, color tags, keywords or smart bins.
Dual-system recording prioritizes synchronization based on time code; when there is no time code, use waveform and spot check the beginning, middle and end.
Proxy media is generated when long GOP or high-resolution footage freezes. The proxy is used for editing and the original film is used for final output.
Create string, featured, and scrap markers for interviews, feature films, or documentaries, preserving original footage.
mistake: Moving the source file in Finder will cause it to go offline; relink it in Resolve when you need to move it.
doneCheck: All media are online, audio and video are synchronized and spot-checked, scenes and shots are searchable, and there are two backups.
proNotes: Proxy, media optimization, and render caching are three different things
Synchronization must check the beginning, middle and end

quickSteps: Watch in full and record questions
proSteps: Create an independent rough cut timeline and avoid overwriting the unique timeline repeatedly.
Choose shots based on scene goals and information advancement, and don’t get obsessed with transitions from the beginning.
Use in-point, out-point and three-point editing to quickly send valid clips to the timeline.
The structure, paragraphs and rhythm are dealt with first, and the sound is only temporarily balanced so that it can be heard clearly.
After each paragraph is completed, read back to the end of the previous paragraph to check whether the emotion can be caught.
Play it all once without interruption, just mark the problem to record it, and make centralized modifications after the playback is over.
mistake: Cutting and toning as you go can mask structural problems and waste time.
doneCheck: The story is understandable from beginning to end, temporary sounds are audible, and questions are tagged by category.
proNotes: The rough cut standard is understandable even if you watch it for the first time
Only record when watching in full without interrupting modifications

quickSteps: Clean up gaps and flickering frames
proSteps: Fine-tune the cut point based on performance and reaction, listen to the sound first, and then decide when to cut the scene.
Use roll, ripple, slip and slide trimming and understand which side each tool changes.
Use J Cut to let the sound of the next shot come first, and use L Cut to let the sound of the previous shot continue to reduce the feeling of hard cutting.
Check motion matching, eye direction, axis, scene changes, and screen orientation.
Zoom into the timeline to check for black frames, overlapping frames, broken transitions, and missing audio.
Make a copy of the version before locking the picture and label it picture lock; subsequent changes must be recorded.
mistake: Improper use of ripple trimming may change the subsequent full-film synchronization, and the total duration of observation after the operation will be changed.
doneCheck: The acting and dialogue have a natural rhythm, there are no flickering frames or gaps, and the frame-locked version has been saved.
proNotes: Hold down K and click J/L to slow down playback
The final round of fine editing should be watched once in blind listening and mute listening.

quickSteps: Musical sound effects give way to dialogue
proSteps: Separate tracks according to DX dialogue, AMB environment, SFX sound effects, and MX music and name them uniformly.
Use clip gain to balance clips first, then use track faders to do the overall mix; don’t pile on plug-ins at the beginning.
Trim hot spots, saliva and obvious noise, cross-fade clip points and fill in the room noise floor.
EQ should first reduce the problem band, and then consider increasing it; compression only needs to control the dynamics, not flatten the dialogue.
Music and sound effects take the initiative to give way when dialogue appears, automating when necessary.
Listen to it with headphones and regular speakers, and see if the level clips.
mistake: Directly applying strong limiting to the main bus may raise the noise floor as well.
doneCheck: Dialogue is always understandable, there are no pops at edit points, the room noise floor is continuous, and the main output doesn't clip.
proNotes: Keep original sync track
Dialogue clarity depends on spectrum and background competition, not just level

quickSteps: Confirm input and output color spaces
Open the oscilloscope and perform first-level calibration
proSteps: Confirm the input color space of each type of camera material to avoid treating Log as Rec.709 or repeated conversion.
First look at the waveform chart, RGB Parade, and vector oscilloscope, and then judge the exposure, color cast, and saturation.
Establish exposure with Offset or HDR global controls, then refine with Lift/Gamma/Gain or Curves.
Choose a hero shot as a reference and match other shots according to the scene. Don’t pursue beauty shot by shot.
Keep selections soft when using qualifiers and windows, and check for motion tracking slippage.
Technical corrections are separated from the style nodes; noise reduction is usually at the front, sharpening and grain at the back.
Check output transforms, color labels, and highlight ranges in a live delivery display environment.
mistake: Applying LUT directly without color management makes it easy to cut highlights, color casts or repeat changes.
doneCheck: Inputs are interpreted correctly, the scope has no unexpected clipping, shots of the same scene match, and output transformations are performed only once.
proNotes: The skin color line is a directional reference rather than an absolute target
Node naming and grouping should be understandable to the person taking over

quickSteps: Check safe box and line breaks
proSteps: First determine the font, font size, line spacing, stroke/baseline, number of words per line, and screen stay rules.
Prioritize placing dialogue subtitles on the subtitle track, do not make each one a Fusion title.
After automatic transcription, names, professional words, numbers and sentence fragments must be proofread sentence by sentence.
Check whether the subtitles are pressed against the character name bar, platform UI or key information on the screen.
Check the safe areas separately in the horizontal and vertical versions, and do not rely on automatic adaptation at the same location.
Before exporting, decide whether to burn subtitles, plug-in SRT, or deliver both at the same time.
mistake: If you only proofread the text without looking at the time, the subtitles will be rushed or trailing.
doneCheck: The names and numbers are correct, the sentences are segmented naturally, there is no overlap, and the burning/plugging method is clear.
proNotes: Natural sentence segmentation is more important than even word segmentation
Platform safety areas should be checked separately for both horizontal and vertical versions.

proSteps: Watch it in its entirety the first time as an audience, recording only issues of understanding, rhythm, and emotion.
A second pass checks for flickering frames, black frames, offline media, screen shake, subtitles, graphics, and copyright marks.
The third time I blindly listened to the sound, and then watched the picture with the sound muted, I found audio and visual continuity issues respectively.
Check first frame, last frame, ending duration, text spelling, date, phone number and brand name.
Check the output test file on at least two players or devices to confirm that gamma and audio and video are in sync.
Simply watching the affected passages again after restoration is not enough; the final master must be watched again in its entirety.
mistake: If you pause the modification as soon as a problem is discovered, you will lose the audience experience of complete viewing.
doneCheck: There are no offline or flickering frames, the subtitle graphics are correct, and the actual exported file has been fully viewed.
proNotes: Create QC lists including timecodes, issues, responsible persons and status
When a frame flashes to black, suspicious editing points need to be reviewed frame by frame.

proSteps: Deduces packaging, encoding, resolution, bitrate, audio and color tags from delivery usage.
Determine whether it is a single clip or individual clips, and whether subtitles, alpha, timecode or stems are required.
Write the project, version, frame, language and date in the file name to avoid calling it just final.mp4.
A short test is output first to check player, platform compression and color display before rendering the full file.
Check the output path, file name, timeline range and preset again after joining the render queue.
Check the final file for length, resolution, audio tracks, subtitles, color and complete playback.
mistake: Forcing the timeline frame rate to the delivery frame rate may produce duplicate frames or cadence changes.
doneCheck: The output range, path, encoding, audio, and subtitles are correct, and the actual file has passed the recheck.
proNotes: Keep high-quality masters first, then generate distribution versions
For player differences, first check the color label and viewing environment

proSteps: Export a project file or project archive and record the Resolve version used.
When using media management to collect actual materials, keep reasonable clip handles and spot-check re-links.
Save high-quality masters, releases, untitled versions, audio tracks, subtitles and key graphics.
Save LUTs, font lists, color management instructions, plug-in lists, and delivery parameters.
Generate README: project content, file structure, final timeline, missing items and recovery steps.
Prove the archive is recoverable by actually opening the project once from the archive location and checking random shots.
mistake: Saving only the DRP without saving the source media does not guarantee long-term recovery.
doneCheck: The project can be opened, the necessary media has been collected, the master and subtitles are complete, and the README and recovery testing have been completed.
proNotes: Archive goals are understandable, verifiable, and recoverable
At least one archive should be physically separated from the work location

scene: First edition of interviews, storylines and promos.
steps: Start with the main paragraph and key events
Use I/O + F9/F10 to complete three-point editing
Only deal with sound problems that hinder understanding
Watch in full and note questions with color markers
risk: Don’t spend time doing final color corrections and complicated transitions in the rough cut stage.
doneCheck: Understandable for first time viewers and all questions are tagged.

scene: The vast majority of narrative cuts.
steps: Source monitor sets I and O
Place the playhead or set a timeline point on the timeline
F9 insert or F10 overwrite
Check target tracks and audiovisual patches
risk: Inserting will change the subsequent position, but overwriting will not; pressing the wrong button will destroy synchronization.
doneCheck: The footage length, placement, and tracks all fit the intent.

scene: Stuck points, action duration adaptation and B-roll.
steps: Source input and output points
Timeline set entry and exit points
Execute Shift+F11
Confirm strategy in speed change prompt
risk: Will change the playback speed, not suitable for dialogue that must maintain true speed.
doneCheck: The start and end points are aligned and the movement speed is acceptable.

steps: Remove or temporarily ignore audio and video links
Extend the left edge of the next audio frame forward
Keep the previous scene and cover this sound
Fill in the crossfade and listen to the room noise floor
risk: Too much advance sound can cause the audience to misunderstand the source of the sound.
doneCheck: The sound guides naturally, and the picture is not abrupt when cutting.

scene: Dialogue reaction shots and interviews B-roll.
steps: Determine the cutting point of the screen first
Extend the right edge of the previous audio audio backwards
Cover the frame with reaction shots
Balance two ambient sounds
risk: Leaving your voice for too long will confuse the relationship between mouth shape and semantics.
doneCheck: The audience still knows who is speaking, and the emotion continues naturally.

scene: Replace lenses and look for front and rear margin.
steps: Select or stop the playhead at the target shot
Execute Match Frame (default F)
View the original film in context in the source monitor
Reset entry and exit points and replace
risk: Verify matching levels when working with multiple cameras, composite clips, or speed changes.
doneCheck: The source monitor is positioned to the same content frame.

scene: Looking for better shows or B-roll.
steps: Move the playhead to the alignment reference frame in the timeline
Source monitor locates the frame you wish to align
Press F11 to replace
Check motion alignment and audio tracks
risk: Replacement is aligned based on the current frame. Wrong position of the source playhead will cause overall misalignment.
doneCheck: Duration remains unchanged and key action frames are aligned.

steps: First use segment gain to bring the subjective loudness closer
Repair explosive spots and obvious noise
Edit point plus very short crossfade
Cover the hole with independent room noise floor
Finally add EQ, compression and moderate noise reduction
risk: Excessive noise reduction can create an underwater and metallic quality.
doneCheck: You can't hear the editing points with your eyes closed, but the words are clear.

steps: Complete editing at normal speed first
Set shift point
Adjust speed and frame position with curves
Choose the right retiming process for slow motion
Check for distortion and ghosting frame by frame
risk: Optical flow may generate false frames at crossing objects, motion blur, and occlusions.
doneCheck: The rhythm is natural, key movements are accurately placed, and there are no obvious artifacts.

steps: Complete lens length and speed first
Analysis Stabilizer
Start with Similarity or Translation
Reduce intensity and check cropping
Check edges and jelly on a frame-by-frame basis
risk: Stronger stabilization is not necessarily better, as it may enlarge the rolling shutter or cause the image to float.
doneCheck: Shake is reduced and movement remains natural, and cropping is acceptable.

scene: Every shot goes into creative color grading.
steps: Confirm input conversion
View Waveform and RGB Parade
Position the whole using Offset/Global Exposure
Refine with Lift/Gamma/Gain or HDR regions
Check saturation and channel clipping
risk: Don’t use black level suppression to create the so-called cinematic feel.
doneCheck: Neutral objects make sense, subjects are clear, and highlights and shadows have intention.

scene: Multiple cameras for plot scenes and interviews.
steps: Select a hero shot and capture a still frame
Turn on split screen or reference wipe
Match the exposure level first
Then match the comprehensive color cast and saturation
Finally deal with local differences
risk: Don't match objects that happen to be different on the screen, match common references and lighting intent.
doneCheck: Viewers will not be interrupted by jumps in brightness or color casts during continuous playback.

scene: Close shot of character, mixed light.
steps: Complete the overall white balance first
Qualifier selects skin and softens keys
Limit area with window and track
Reference skin color direction on vectorscope
Review mask edges and motion
risk: The skin tone line is not an absolute goal; differences should be preserved for different skin tones and lighting.
doneCheck: The skin is natural, the selection is stable, and there is no obvious pollution in the background.

steps: 01 Noise reduction (when needed)
02 Input/Exposure
03 White balance and matching
04 skin color/local
05 Look
06 Trimming before output
Output transformation is the responsibility of project management or independent nodes.
risk: Project-level color management and CST nodes do not perform output transformations repeatedly.
doneCheck: The nodes are clearly named so that any layer of the bypass can understand their role.

scene: Brighten the face, darken the background, and correct partial color casts.
steps: Create a Soft Power Window
Start by setting the shape and feathering on a representative frame
Forward and reverse tracking
Check occlusion and draw out
Correct drift keyframes piece by piece
risk: If the window is too hard or the brightness is too strong, it will look like a stage chasing light.
doneCheck: At normal speed, the edge of the window cannot be seen, and the tracking does not drift.

scene: High ISO, enhanced shadows, unified style.
steps: Do time domain noise reduction first if necessary
A small amount of spatial noise reduction processing remains
Complete main color grading
Slight sharpening or mid-frequency detail
Finally, add particles to unify the texture
risk: Studio's noise reduction is very heavy, and if the parameters are too high, the skin texture will be lost and the rendering will be slowed down.
doneCheck: Pause and play are natural, without smear, waxiness or sharp edges.

scene: Screen lock and before final output.
steps: Watch the story for the first time without interruption
Check the technology and text item by item for the second time
Blindly listen to the sound for the third time and then watch the picture with mute
Problem unified recording time code
Watch it again after repair
risk: If you make changes while watching, you will lose the entire movie experience and easily miss follow-up questions.
doneCheck: The list is all closed and the final file is viewed in its entirety and passed.

steps: Export DRP/DRA
Media management collects and uses materials and titles
Save masters, subtitles and audio tracks
Attached is a list of LUTs, fonts and plug-ins
Write a README and do random recovery testing
risk: Posting only MP4s does not count as an archive.
doneCheck: Another machine or a clean path can be opened and reconnected.

steps: Determine the input color space for each type of camera
Choosing a technology path between RCM and CST
Make sure the output transformation is only executed once
doneCheck: Log, RAW and Rec.709 footage are all interpreted correctly.
risk: Superposition of RCM and node CST results in repeated transformations.
commonMistakes: RCM and CST repeated output transformations

steps: Open Waveform, RGB Parade and Vectorscope
First use Offset/HDR to establish overall exposure
Then use Lift/Gamma/Gain or curve to refine
doneCheck: The subject is clear and the channel has no unexpected clipping.
risk: Crushing black levels is not cinematic.
commonMistakes: Don’t use an oscilloscope, just rely on the display to judge

steps: Select a hero shot and grab a still
Match the exposure level first
Then match the comprehensive color cast and saturation
doneCheck: There is no obvious brightness or color shift jump during continuous playback.
risk: Match common references and lighting intentions rather than different objects in the frame.
commonMistakes: Match objects that happen to be different in the picture
Each pursues good looks shot by shot

steps: After the overall white balance is completed, the skin color is limited
Soften keys and limit areas with windows
Check edges and motion after tracking
doneCheck: The skin is natural, the selection is stable, and the background is free from contamination.
risk: The skin color line is a reference direction and is not the same target for everyone.
commonMistakes: Treat the skin tone line as an absolute goal
Key or window edges are too hard

steps: Put noise reduction at the front when needed
Separate Exposure, Match, Local and Look nodes
Name nodes and bypass comparison
doneCheck: Bypassing any layer can understand its role.
risk: Don't mix project-level output management into Look nodes.
commonMistakes: Technical corrections are mixed in the same node as Look
Project-level output management mixed into Look nodes

steps: Mainly toning and then a small amount of sharpening
Finally, add particles to unify the texture
Check color labels, highlights and target display environment
doneCheck: Play and pause are natural, and the output labels are correct.
risk: Excessive noise reduction can lose skin texture and slow down rendering.
commonMistakes: Excessive noise reduction causes waxy feeling or smearing
Color labels not checked in target display environment

specificationValues: 1920×1080 or the original frame of the project
About 8–16 Mb/s, do a short test first
risk: Chat software can perform secondary compression; important film review also provides file transfer methods.
bitrate: H.264 ~8–16 Mb/s; do a short video test first
subtitles: The review version can be burned with temporary subtitles or additional SRT, which must be marked in the review instructions.
fileChecks: Play actual file in full
Check file name, version and date
Check resolution, frame rate, and AAC sound
Randomly check each of the chat software and file transfer method.

specificationValues: Use the recommended range of the platform, and increase the 4K appropriately.
risk: Do not forcefully change the frame rate for the platform; high-quality uploading can reduce secondary compression losses.
bitrate: Set according to target platform recommended range; 4K usually requires higher bitrates
subtitles: Burn, embed or upload subtitle files separately according to platform requirements; confirm language and default track.
fileChecks: Play actual file in full
Check the resolution and frame rate before uploading to the platform
Check audio, color labels and subtitle tracks
Upload short test and check platform transcoding

specificationValues: Maintain master timeline or delivery appointments
About 10–20 Mb/s, measured on the platform
risk: Check refactoring, subtitles, and platform UI safe areas separately, can't just auto-crop landscape.
bitrate: H.264 approximately 10–20 Mb/s; subject to short measurement on target platform
subtitles: Subtitles must avoid the safe area of ​​the vertical platform UI; the burning and plug-in methods must be clear.
fileChecks: Play actual file in full
Check 9:16 Frame and Safe Area
Check subtitles, audio and reconstructed footage
Short test on target platform

specificationValues: 10-bit or higher, by source and delivery
Identify Rec.709, P3 or other master space
risk: The master space must be written in the filename or README; don't just keep H.264.
bitrate: Determined by ProRes/DNxHR encoding gear, no manual setting of target code rate is required
subtitles: Save masters with and without subtitles, and save subtitle files separately.
fileChecks: Play actual file in full
Check master color space and 10-bit specifications
Check PCM sounds and channels
Check file name, version, date and README

specificationValues: XML/AAF + original film, or high-quality flat film
Original media first; ProRes 4444/DNxHR 444 for plain film
No baking creative coloring, unless agreed upon
risk: Start by checking with your colorist about delivery methods, frames, shifting, reframing, subtitling, and Fusion processing.
bitrate: There is no target bitrate for original media; high-quality flat films are determined by intermediate encoding levels
subtitles: Know whether to deliver a subtitles track, a burned reference version, or a separate SRT to avoid having subtitles baked into the image being graded.
fileChecks: Check XML/AAF and media can be opened
Check credits, timecode, speed shifting and reconstruction
Check Reference Mix WAV
Spot check re-linking and color management instructions

specificationValues: Based on channel specifications as the only basis
According to XDCAM, DNxHD and other conventions
Meet the legal level and code rate
Channel layout, loudness and peaking as per specification
risk: The latest technical specifications, loudness and opening and closing requirements must be obtained.
bitrate: Determined by the latest technical specifications of the channel and the specified encoding configuration
subtitles: Subtitle delivery method and language version are subject to channel technical specifications.
fileChecks: Play actual file in full
Check packaging, bit rate and legal level according to channel specifications
Check loudness and channel layout
Check the playlist file name and subtitle requirements

specificationValues: Usually 24/25 and other support files, according to theater and master
Correct conversion from controlled master to XYZ
risk: DCP must be fully QC in a professional player or theater; encryption, KDM, sound channels and frames must be agreed in advance.
bitrate: Determined by DCP delivery specifications, format and theater QC requirements
subtitles: Subtitles should use theater-agreed burned or optional subtitle tracks and correspond to the DCP package version.
fileChecks: Complete QC in Professional Player
Check frame, frame rate, XYZ and JPEG 2000
Check multichannel mapping
Check encryption, KDM and naming conventions

risk: H.264 does not support regular alpha; check edges when new items are layered onto a color background before delivery.
bitrate: Determined by ProRes 4444/DNxHR 444 gear or PNG image sequence
subtitles: Graphic elements usually do not include subtitle tracks; if text is included, text versions and font descriptions should be delivered.
fileChecks: Check Alpha Edge on Color Base
Check Thru/Pre-Ride Instructions
Check frame rate, size and encoding
Play actual file in full

cause: Drive letter/volume name changes, material movement, proxy path failure or codec unavailability.
fix: Confirm that the material disk is mounted and the volume name has not changed
Select offline clips in media pool > Relink selected clips
If only the agent is offline, switch back to the original media or relocate the agent
deep: Check file extensions, camera raw directories, system decoding support, and path case.
prevent: Move media within the project or use media to manage archives without changing the path in the Finder.

cause: High compression, long GOP, special effects, noise reduction, slow cache disk or too high resolution.
fix: Confirm that it is not background rendering or the disk is full
Playback > Timeline proxy resolution changed to half/quarter
Generate proxy media; complex special effects use render cache
deep: Distinguish between decoding, GPU, and disk bottlenecks; turn off noise reduction for itemized exclusions.
prevent: A proxy is used in the editing stage, and the final output is back to the original film; the cache is used to play the high-speed disk independently.

cause: Recording sample rate, variable frame rate mobile footage, incorrect frame rate explanation or sync point error.
fix: Confirm timeline frame rate and material interpretation
Mobile phone VFR material is first converted to constant frame rate intermediate code
Use the three points of the head, middle and tail to determine whether there is a fixed offset or continuous drift
deep: A fixed offset allows for overall movement; continued drift requires resampling or fine-tuning the speed.
prevent: Shoot and plate with unified timecode/sample rate, and check VFR before mobile phone footage is put into storage.

cause: Color tags, viewer gamma, display color management, or duplicate/missing output transformations.
fix: Confirm that the output only undergoes a Rec.709 transformation
Check Export Color Space/Gamma Tag
Compare with controlled player and oscilloscope
deep: First distinguish between file data errors and display differences.
prevent: Establish short test files and target platform test procedures to record project color management.

cause: Proxy filename/timecode mismatch, wrong path, or output settings force proxy use.
fix: Media pool checks proxy path and metadata
Relink the correct files after deagent
Delivery advanced settings confirm not using proxy media
deep: Spot-check the first frame, duration, frame rate, audio track and time code of the proxy and original film.
prevent: Unify proxy defaults and naming, eliminating the need for low-code files from unknown sources.

cause: Cache corruption, insufficient location space, or node cache not invalidated.
fix: Confirm that the cache disk is writable and has space
Play > Delete Render Cache > All or Selected Clips
Switch cache mode and regenerate if necessary
deep: Don't delete source material by mistake; just clear the CacheClip or manage it via the Resolve menu.
prevent: Cache an independent directory and clean it regularly. The cache will not be used as an archive when the project is finished.

cause: The subtitle export mode is not selected for burning, the external subtitles are not delivered separately, or the subtitle track is disabled.
fix: Delivery page chooses to burn to video or export subtitles file
Confirm that the correct subtitle track is enabled
Output 20 second test and verify on target player
deep: Clarify the three delivery methods of burning, embedding, and plug-in.
prevent: The delivery list lists subtitle mode, language and file name separately.

cause: Bad frames, plug-in, Fusion, VRAM, disk space or encoder issues.
fix: Record the failure timecode and check around that frame
Temporarily bypass complex special effects/noise reduction positioning issues
First output the ProRes/DNxHR intermediate master, and then convert it to the distribution format
deep: For fixed positions, more consideration should be given to materials or special effects; for position changes, more consideration should be given to resources or hardware.
prevent: For long films, do short tests first; leave margins on the cache disk and output disk.

cause: Bus assignments, tracks muted, output audio unchecked, or channel mapping wrong.
fix: Delivery page confirmation Export Audio
Fairlight checks track to bus routing
Check bus format and export channel settings
deep: Multi-channel delivery requires bus-by-bus, track format and file channel mapping confirmation.
prevent: Save presets for reliable delivery and check your channels with actual files.

cause: A frame gap between clips, insufficient transitions, offline frames, or speed effects boundaries.
fix: Use the up and down arrow keys to jump to the clip point
Check frame by frame with left and right arrow keys
Zoom into the timeline and remove gaps or adjust transition margins
deep: If there are no gaps in the timeline, check for source file corruption, optical flow, or Fusion boundaries.
prevent: Perform clip-by-clip QC and black frame detection before locking the picture.

cause: Real-time saving/backup is not enabled, or the only timeline is always overwritten.
fix: Right-click the project in the project manager to view the backup
Restore the latest stable backup and save the new version
Check timeline backup and auto-save locations
deep: Copy the project first after recovery to avoid overwriting versions that are still available.
prevent: Real-time saving + project backup + key node copy timeline.

cause: Third-party plug-ins, fonts, LUTs or DCTLs are not archived with the project.
fix: View missing item hints and record names
Install legal resources of the same version
Rebuild with master reference and mark differences if recovery is not possible
deep: Changes in the plug-in version will also change the results, and you cannot just record the plug-in name.
prevent: Archive font lists, plug-in versions, LUT/DCTL and key effects screenshots.
